Online Bayesian change point detection (onlineBcp)

Source: R/dfr_onlinebcp.R
online_bcp.Rd

Online Bayesian change point detection for normal data of Yigiter et al. (2015), as implemented in the R package onlineBcp (Xu, Yigiter and Chen, 2022). The time since the last change (run length) follows a Markov chain with geometric hazard (1 - theta is the probability of a change at each step), and the segments are normal with a normal-inverse-gamma prior on their mean and variance. At every step the posterior of the last change point location is updated; when its largest value exceeds threshold, that location becomes the last change point and the search restarts from it.

Usage

online_bcp(
  x,
  theta = 0.9,
  alpha = 1,
  beta = 1,
  threshold = 0.5,
  numerics = c("stable", "reference"),
  normality = FALSE
)

Arguments

x

A numeric vector without missing values.

theta

Probability that no change occurs at a step.

alpha, beta

Hyperparameters of the inverse-gamma prior of the variance.

threshold

Threshold of the posterior probability (th_cp).

numerics

"stable" (default) computes the weights in log scale with lgamma(). "reference" computes them as onlineBcp 0.1.4 does, with gamma() and powers that overflow for segments longer than about 340 observations; the overflowing weights are set to 0, which forces change points at multiples of about 341 observations (see Details).

normality

TRUE adds the Kolmogorov-Smirnov normality test of each segment.

Value

An online_bcp object: changepoints (location, the last observation before the change, and its posterior probability), segments (begin, end, mean, SD, interval limits and, optionally, the normality p-value), and trace, one row per step with the largest posterior probability (max_prob), the location (location, 0 when below the threshold) and the run of equal locations (run), as max_p of onlineBcp.

Details

The update follows online_cp() of onlineBcp 0.1.4 (https://github.com/ElsevierSoftwareX/SOFTX-D-21-00221). At time t, for every candidate location j from the last change point tau to t,

  • j < t: w = Gamma(u + 1/2) / Gamma(u) * sqrt((t - j + 1) / (t - j + 2)) * (A + 2 beta)^u / (B + 2 beta)^(u + 1/2) / sqrt(pi), u = (t - j + 2 alpha) / 2, with A and B the centred sums of squares of x[(j + 1):t] and x[(j + 1):(t + 1)] (with denominators t - j + 1 and t - j + 2), and P(R = j) = w theta P_prev(R = j);

  • j = t: w = 2^alpha Gamma(alpha + 1/2) / (sqrt(2 pi) (x[t + 1]^2 / 2 + beta)^(alpha + 1/2)), and P(R = t) = w (1 - theta) sum(P_prev).

The code differs from Eq. 3 of the paper in the weight of a new segment, (x^2 / 2 + beta) where the paper writes (x^2 / 2 + 2 beta); the code is followed. With numerics = "reference", gamma() overflows when (t - j + 2 alpha + 1) / 2 exceeds about 171.6, and the weight, then NaN or Inf, is set to 0 as in the code. The change points of the paper's aCGH example at 341, 682 and 1023 come from this overflow; "stable" avoids it.

The segments are built as summary.BayesCP() does. A change point is a location whose posterior exceeds threshold at a step where the location differs from that of the previous step. Segments of one observation are merged with the previous segment of more than one, or with the next one at the start. The interval of each segment mean is mean +- qnorm(0.95) sd / sqrt(n) (a 90% interval; the paper calls it 95%). With normality = TRUE, the p-value of the Kolmogorov-Smirnov test of each segment against the normal distribution with its mean and standard deviation is added.

The cost of a step grows with the time since the last change point, so a long sequence without changes takes quadratic time.

References

Yigiter, A., Chen, J., An, L. and Danacioglu, N. (2015). An on-line CNV detection method for short sequencing reads. Journal of Applied Statistics, 42(7), 1556-1571. doi:10.1080/02664763.2014.1001330

Xu, H., Yigiter, A. and Chen, J. (2022). onlineBcp: An R package for online change point detection using a Bayesian approach. SoftwareX, 17, 100999. doi:10.1016/j.softx.2022.100999

See also

dfr_onlinebcp() to monitor a stream.

Examples

set.seed(1)
x <- c(stats::rnorm(100, 0), stats::rnorm(100, 3), stats::rnorm(100, 0))
result <- online_bcp(x, theta = 0.95, threshold = 0.7)
result$changepoints
#>   location post.prob
#> 1      100 0.7204097
result$segments
#>   begin end      mean        SD    LL of CI UL of CI
#> 1     1 100 0.1088874 0.8981994 -0.03885328 0.256628
#> 2   101 300 1.4959327 1.7746395  1.28952669 1.702339
